verdict.rationale: Browserbase markets this use case directly: it says it can "Track prices, job listings, product changes, and competitor moves as they happen". It also documents scheduled agent runs and outbound webhooks for subscribed events, which together support recurring checks with programmatic delivery. However, the evidence never documents a built-in change-detection or diffing feature, nor a webhook event that fires on page-content changes; the webhooks are framed around status changes. Missing for 10: documented content-change or diff detection, a webhook or notification event tied to detected content changes, and hands-on or independent corroboration of monitoring workflows.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can monitor target pages for content changes, such as price or listing updates, and get notified as they happen

citations.quote: Track prices, job listings, product changes, and competitor moves as they happen.
Deploy and run browser agents on Browserbase, on a schedule or on demand.
Browserbase webhooks send an HTTP POST to an endpoint you own as soon as a subscribed event happens, so you don't have to poll the API for status changes.
